BiblicalUsage: Blasting is the wind that burns the crop in the ear. Solomon prays that when famine and pestilence and blasting come, God will hear from heaven, and the prophets say God smote Israel with blasting and mildew and hail, yet they turned not to Him. The king of Assyria's messenger mocks the inhabitants of Judah as corn blasted before it be grown up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe blasting is judgment a farmer understands. The crop stands and then it is gone, and I hold that God sends such losses to turn a people back, not to leave them with nothing.
